on_8_the_fin_wall.blurb: A steep sport-leaning wall within the Lion's Head cliffs on the Bruce Peninsula, with about a dozen bolted lines and a few trad ones. This is a hard-climber's venue: apart from one very easy line, everything runs from 5.11 up, with 5.11 and 5.12 split about evenly, plus two 5.13s and a lone 5.14. Several routes begin from the ground and a few start at hanging belays. The setting is quiet forest above the escarpment edge, and the walk to the base is short once you are down the gully from the top. Expect technical, sustained single-pitch climbing rather than a place for building mileage.

on_9j_titan_wall.blurb: The Titan Wall is a sport-only wall at Lion's Head on the Bruce Peninsula, with routes aimed squarely at strong climbers. Of its fourteen lines, only one or two sit around 5.10 and 5.11; the rest are 5.12 to 5.14, and six of them are 5.14. Lines here are among the longest and hardest at the Head, and most start from the ground. Expect an imposing, vertical wall with technical climbing that rewards footwork and balance over brute power, plus views over Georgian Bay. You reach it from the clifftop, either by walking down the gully or by rappelling, so it is not a casual outing.

on_the_alley.blurb: The Alley is a sub-area of Old Baldy, the Beaver Valley sport cliff above the village of Kimberley. It holds about fourteen routes, nearly all of them bolted, with one trad line. The grades run from 5.6 to 5.11 and cluster in the 5.10s, so it suits climbers stepping up from moderates as well as those wanting a warm-up. The lines run along a narrow, crevice-like cave formation rather than an open face. A couple of its routes, such as an easy 5.7 and a 5.10 favourite, are among the better-regarded lines here.
